caption:
A false positive costs more than the fuel to check it. It costs the credibility of the next alert.

Send a team to a site three times on a signature that turns out to be nothing — a sun-warmed rooftop, a herd, a barge — and the fourth alert gets a slower response, whatever the actual case. That drift starts quiet and compounds fast.

The fix isn't fewer alerts. It's ground-truthing the model against confirmed incidents until the threshold reflects what actually matters, not what technically triggers. An alert that isn't worth the trip is a cost — but the real cost lands later, in the alert nobody believed.

card.headline: The real cost of a false alarm
card.sub: It isn't the wasted trip. It's the next alert nobody trusts. Thresholds have to be tuned against confirmed outcomes, not just triggers.
